Hi Rachel — welcome and thanks for the clear summary. We're excited about the opportunity to embed Redwood into LumenFlow. Quick answers up front and a proposed next step:

- Yes, we support OEM-style on-premise / private deployments and a bundled-server model for partners. We call the package Redwood Private (OEM variant).
- Commercials: we can do fixed instance pricing (monthly), enterprise seat-based, or a blended revenue share — details depend on expected volume and whether you want managed updates.
- Co-branding: we have a partner branding guide. Light co-branding (partner logo + "powered by Redwood") is standard; full white-label (no Redwood branding) requires an enterprise license and a separate legal addendum.
- Data flows: telemetry can be restricted. For Private deployments, customer data can stay in your VPC; we offer an audited DPA/KMS integration.
- SLA: Dedicated SLAs available; we also can provide a support entitlement for your customers via a partner-support bundle.

Next step: Sched 45m with our product and legal leads. Vanessa (partnerships) will coordinate. I've attached a short term sheet draft to start the commercial conversation. Can you do Thu 5th or Mon 9th PST?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Markus / Vanessa — quick technical notes to bring into the call:

1) Deployment model options
   - Private VPC bundle: recommended for enterprise customers who want data residency and zero egress. Requires a light config manager on your side but minimal runtime changes.
   - On-prem container: we provide an air-gapped install. Update cadence is quarterly unless you elect managed updates.

2) Runtime constraints / performance
   - If LumenFlow wants a responsive in-UI experience (sub-300ms median for small prompts) we should lock to a smaller local model variant (e.g., 4B/8B) and enable quantization. For longer-form generation, route to a hosted Redwood endpoint with fallback.

3) Telemetry & logging
   - We can disable prompt logging and only surface aggregated usage metrics. However, for abuse detection and model health we recommend opt-in telemetry that can be routed to LumenFlow's monitoring endpoints.

4) Security questions to confirm on the kickoff
   - SSO/SAML integration for admin portal, KMS key exchange, and audit log retention period.

I'll prepare a short checklist (install footprint, GPU/CPU guidance, supported runtimes) before the call.

— Karthik
Product Lead, Embedded Partner Tech

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood OEM — initial ask (embedding + co-branding)

Team — high-level legal flags to expect for conversation with LumenFlow:

- IP / Sublicense: LumenFlow will likely want the right to redistribute the runtime as part of their product. We should offer a limited sublicense grant tied to the territory and supported customer types.
- Data processing: require a DPA with clear data controller/processor roles. For Private deployments, clarify that Redwood processes no customer PII unless explicitly enabled.
- Indemnity & liability caps: propose a scaled cap — higher for revenue-share models, lower for fixed-fee licensing.
- Branding: full white-label must require a fee and explicit approval of UI assets.

I'll prepare suggested language and a redline template for the term sheet. If they push aggressive sublicensing, we can propose a rev-share + annual audit clause instead.

— Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
